## Scope and provenance

This document is the mathematical specification of the **ATLS** thermal-response
layer added to the TF24 leaf model (issue #566), building on the Penman–Monteith
leaf energy balance (#523). It describes the equations *as implemented* on the
branch `feature/tf24-atls-thermal-damage`, cross-referenced to the source:

- Leaf-level physics and kinetics: [`src/leaf_model.cpp`](../src/leaf_model.cpp),
  [`inst/include/plant/leaf_model.h`](../inst/include/plant/leaf_model.h).
- Acclimation state dynamics and whole-plant costs:
  [`src/tf24t_strategy.cpp`](../src/tf24t_strategy.cpp),
  [`inst/include/plant/models/tf24t_strategy.h`](../inst/include/plant/models/tf24t_strategy.h).

The layer is **gated** (`use_thermal_damage_`): with the gate off, every equation
below collapses to its TF24 form (no lasting damage, no $T_\mathrm{opt}$ shift, no
thermal cost), so base TF24 (and TF24+PM) remain bit-identical. The `TF24t` strategy
turns the gate on unconditionally and, because the damage substrate is only
physically meaningful at a real operating-point leaf temperature, also forces the PM
energy balance on.

This document describes the model **as implemented after the merged revision**
(§[-@sec-merged]): the two reversible high-temperature declines are unified onto one
Medlyn deactivation curve, and damage is given lasting memory through two slow pools
$I_r$ (recoverable) and $I_p$ (permanent). The companion `TF24t_leaf_ATLS_demo.qmd`
exercises these equations numerically; this document states them.

Notation: temperatures are in °C unless written $T_K = T + T_0$ with
$T_0 = 273.15$. $R = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$ is the gas constant.

---

## The model in one paragraph

A leaf sits at an operating temperature $T_\ell$ set by its energy balance
(§[-@sec-energy]). Photosynthetic *capacity* ($V_\mathrm{cmax}$, $J_\mathrm{max}$)
follows a reversible peaked-Arrhenius response whose optimum $T_\mathrm{opt}$ can be
shifted up by constitutive tolerance and by acclimation (§[-@sec-capacity]). The
high-temperature deactivation term of that *same* curve defines a transiently
**unfolded fraction** $\varphi_d(T_\ell)$ (§[-@sec-damage]); a fraction of that
unfolded protein leaks into **lasting damage**, carried by two slow ODE pools — a
recoverable pool $I_r$ (resynthesised over days) and a permanent pool $I_p$ (cleared
only as the plant grows new leaf). Both capacities carry the lasting discount
$(1-I_r-I_p)$. Damage onset is *emergent* at $\approx H_d/\Delta S \approx 34.5$ °C
from the deactivation thermodynamics, not a separate parameter. Constitutive
tolerance and a single inducible acclimation state $A$ shift $\Delta S$ (moving
$T_\mathrm{opt}$ and the onset together; §[-@sec-accl]). Every axis carries a carbon
cost (§[-@sec-cost]). Because $\varphi_d$ (and the capacity) are evaluated at the
operating-point $T_\ell$, transpirational cooling (**avoidance**) reduces the damage
flux and is self-selecting in the stomatal/hydraulic optimiser (§[-@sec-feedback]).

The four strategy axes map onto the equations as:

| Axis | Parameter(s) | Enters via |
|---|---|---|
| **Tolerance** (constitutive) | $\Delta T_\mathrm{opt,0}$ (`topt_offset`) | thermostability shift of $\Delta S$ → $T_\mathrm{opt}$ and onset (§[-@sec-topt-shift]) |
| **Acclimation** (inducible) | $A$ (ODE state) | same $\Delta S$ shift, inducibly (§[-@sec-accl]) |
| **Repair** | preventive $k_i$, restorative $k_\mathrm{rec}$ | the $I_r$ cascade (§[-@sec-damage]) |
| **Avoidance** | transpiration $E$ via PM | $T_\ell$ → $\varphi_d$ (§[-@sec-energy], §[-@sec-feedback]) |

---

## Leaf temperature: Penman–Monteith energy balance {#sec-energy}

The operating leaf temperature is the explicit (minimal-cut) energy balance from
#523 ([`leaf_model.cpp:1178`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L1178)):

$$
T_\ell \;=\; T_\mathrm{air} \;+\; \frac{\left(R_n - \lambda E\right)\, r_a}{\rho c_p},
\qquad T_\ell \in [-40, 70]\ \text{°C (clamped)} .
$$ {#eq-tleaf}

The incoming `air_temp` driver (read via `TF24_Environment::get_air_temp()`) is
the air temperature $T_\mathrm{air}$. The terms are:

- **Net radiation** ([`leaf_model.cpp:249`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L249)):
  $$
  R_n \;=\; \frac{a_\mathrm{sw}\,Q}{\eta_\mathrm{par}} \;+\; L_\mathrm{net},
  $$
  with absorbed PAR $Q$ (`PPFD_`, µmol m⁻² s⁻¹), shortwave-to-PAR factor
  $a_\mathrm{sw}=2$, PAR photon conversion $\eta_\mathrm{par}=4.57$ µmol J⁻¹, and a
  fixed clear-sky longwave cooling offset $L_\mathrm{net}=-40$ W m⁻².
- **Aerodynamic resistance** from leaf boundary-layer theory
  ([`leaf_model.cpp:254`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L254)):
  $$
  r_a \;=\; C_{r_a}\sqrt{\frac{d}{U}} \quad (C_{r_a}=200),
  $$
  with leaf dimension $d$ and above-canopy wind speed $U$; a fixed
  $r_a = 50$ s m⁻¹ is used when $d$ or $U$ is unusable. Smaller $d$ / higher $U$
  ⇒ better coupling ⇒ $T_\ell$ closer to $T_\mathrm{air}$.
- **Latent heat** $\lambda = 2.45\times10^{6}$ J kg⁻¹; **volumetric heat capacity of
  air** $\rho c_p = 1200$ J m⁻³ K⁻¹.
- **Transpiration** $E$ (kg H₂O m⁻² s⁻¹) is *not* free: it is pinned by the existing
  Sperry hydraulic supply at the stem water potential $\psi_\mathrm{stem}$ chosen by
  the profit optimiser (§[-@sec-feedback]).

> **Caveat (minimal-cut PM).** With $r_a$ fixed and no leaf-to-air VPD feedback, an
> isolated leaf under high radiation overheats several °C above air. Absolute $T_\ell$
> is therefore an upper bound; the *contrast* between well- and poorly-coupled leaves
> is the robust signal (see `notes/atls/gate-atls-vs-pm-evaluation.md`).

The operating-point $T_\ell$ solved here is retained on the leaf as `Leaf::T_op_`
and exported by TF24t as the aux `operating_leaf_temp`, so downstream states (the
running mean, §[-@sec-accl]) and diagnostics can read the temperature the leaf
actually ran at, not just the air-temperature driver.

---

## Reversible photosynthetic capacity {#sec-capacity}

### Arrhenius and peaked-Arrhenius forms

Temperature-independent-optimum parameters ($\Gamma^*$, $K_o$, $K_c$) use a plain
Arrhenius response ([`leaf_model.cpp:1050`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L1050)):

$$
f_\mathrm{arrh}(T_\ell; E_a, f_{25})
= f_{25}\,\exp\!\left[\frac{E_a\,(T_{\ell,K}-298.15)}{298.15\,R\,T_{\ell,K}}\right].
$$

$V_\mathrm{cmax}$ and $J_\mathrm{max}$ use the Medlyn (2002) **peaked**-Arrhenius form,
which adds a high-temperature deactivation term
([`leaf_model.cpp:1056`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L1056)):

$$
f_\mathrm{peak}(T_\ell; E_a, f_{25}, H_d, \Delta S)
= f_\mathrm{arrh}(T_\ell)\cdot
\frac{1+\exp\!\big[(\Delta S\cdot 298.15 - H_d)/(298.15\,R)\big]}
     {1+\exp\!\big[(\Delta S\cdot T_{\ell,K} - H_d)/(R\,T_{\ell,K})\big]}.
$$ {#eq-peak}

The peak location (capacity optimum) is

$$
T_{\mathrm{opt},K} \;=\; \frac{H_d}{\Delta S - R\ln\!\big(E_a/(H_d-E_a)\big)} .
$$ {#eq-topt}

Defaults ($V_\mathrm{cmax}$: $E_a=60000$, $H_d=200000$, $\Delta S=650$;
$J_\mathrm{max}$: $E_a=30000$, $H_d=200000$, $\Delta S=650$ — all J mol⁻¹, J mol⁻¹,
J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹) place $T_\mathrm{opt}\approx30$ °C. $\Delta S$ is the knob that moves it:
lower $\Delta S$ ⇒ higher $T_\mathrm{opt}$.

### Shifting the optimum: $T_\mathrm{opt}$ target → $\Delta S$ inversion {#sec-topt-shift}

Rather than exposing $\Delta S$, the model exposes a **target optimum shift**
$\Delta T_\mathrm{opt}$ (°C) and inverts @eq-topt for the $\Delta S$ that achieves it
([`leaf_model.cpp:1093`](../src/leaf_model.cpp#L1093)). With
$\mathrm{corr}=R\ln(E_a/(H_d-E_a))$ and baseline optimum
$T_{\mathrm{opt},0,K}=H_d/(\Delta S_\mathrm{base}-\mathrm{corr})$:

$$
T_{\mathrm{opt},K}' = \mathrm{clamp}\!\big(T_{\mathrm{opt},0,K} + \Delta T_\mathrm{opt},\;250,\;350\big),
\qquad
\Delta S' = \frac{H_d}{T_{\mathrm{opt},K}'} + \mathrm{corr}.
$$

The clamp on $T_{\mathrm{opt},K}'$ keeps the curve peaked and finite for any offset.
The total shift combines the constitutive (tolerance) offset and a *single*
inducible thermostability state $A$ (§[-@sec-accl]):

$$
\Delta T_\mathrm{opt} \;=\; \underbrace{\Delta T_\mathrm{opt,0}}_{\text{tolerance}}
\;+\; \underbrace{\Delta T_{\mathrm{opt,max}}\,\frac{A}{A+K_A}}_{\text{acclimation}} .
$$ {#eq-dtopt}

$\Delta S'$ (from $\Delta T_\mathrm{opt}$) is applied to *both* $V_\mathrm{cmax}$ and
$J_\mathrm{max}$ in @eq-peak. The same shift moves the damage onset (§[-@sec-damage]),
so raising thermostability translates the whole thermal response up in temperature —
one knob, near-rigid (the small correction term of @eq-topt makes peak and onset move
by *nearly*, not exactly, the same amount; see §[-@sec-merged-numerics]).

---

## Thermal damage: the unfolded fraction $\varphi_d$ and two lasting pools {#sec-damage}

### The single reversible deactivation equilibrium {#sec-phid}

The Medlyn denominator of @eq-peak already encodes a two-state
active⇌deactivated equilibrium. Its constant $K(T_\ell)$ and the deactivated
(unfolded) fraction are ([`leaf_model.cpp`](../src/leaf_model.cpp),
`deactivated_fraction`):

$$
K(T_\ell)=\exp\!\left[\frac{\Delta S\,T_{\ell,K} - H_d}{R\,T_{\ell,K}}\right],
\qquad
\varphi_d(T_\ell)=\frac{K}{1+K},\qquad
\varphi_a(T_\ell)=\frac{1}{1+K}=1-\varphi_d .
$$ {#eq-phid}

This is the *same* $K(T_\ell)$ that sits in `peak_arrh_curve`, so the reversible
capacity curve is unchanged ($f_\mathrm{peak}=f_\mathrm{arrh}\,[1+K(25)]\,\varphi_a$);
$\varphi_d$ is a byproduct of it, evaluated at the midday operating-point $T_\ell$.
Two consequences follow for free:

- **Damage onset is emergent, not a parameter.** Half-unfolding ($K=1$) sits at
  $T_K=H_d/\Delta S = 200000/650 \approx 34.5$ °C, a few degrees above
  $T_\mathrm{opt}$, both from the *same* $(H_d,\Delta S)$. The as-built `tcrit_0`,
  `m_switch`, `dTcrit_max` are gone.
- **One curve drives both capacities.** $\varphi_d$ depends only on $H_d,\Delta S$
  (identical for $V_\mathrm{cmax}$ and $J_\mathrm{max}$); the implementation uses one
  $\Delta S$, shifted by acclimation via the onset $H_d/\Delta S$
  (`d_S_damage_shifted`, Ea-independent so the shift is a near-rigid translation).

### The damage cascade: recoverable $I_r$ and permanent $I_p$ {#sec-cascade}

Fractions of the original machinery sum to 1: active $(1-I_r-I_p)\varphi_a$,
transiently unfolded $(1-I_r-I_p)\varphi_d$ (refolds on cooling; leaks to $I_r$),
recoverable-inactivated $I_r$, permanent $I_p$. **Both** capacities carry the lasting
discount ([`leaf_model.cpp`](../src/leaf_model.cpp),
`update_temperature_dependent_params`):

$$
V_\mathrm{cmax}=f_\mathrm{peak}^{V}(T_\ell)\,(1-I_r-I_p),
\qquad
J_\mathrm{max}=f_\mathrm{peak}^{J}(T_\ell)\,(1-I_r-I_p).
$$ {#eq-discount}

(The reversible $\varphi_a$ is already inside $f_\mathrm{peak}$, so there is no double
discount. The survival fraction $1-I_r-I_p$ is floored at a negligible
$10^{-6}$ so capacity stays strictly positive and the photosynthesis / $\psi$-stem
solve is well-conditioned as $I_r+I_p\to1$.) The two pools are **slow ODE states on
the strategy** (§[-@sec-accl]); at a single fresh evaluation ($I_r=I_p=0$) a hot leaf
loses nothing instantly beyond the reversible $\varphi_a$ — damage is a *memory* that
accrues over time, unlike the as-built instantaneous factor.

$J_\mathrm{max}$ (after the discount) sets the light-limited electron transport rate
via the unchanged non-rectangular hyperbola, colimiting with the Rubisco-limited rate
in the TF24 FvCB solver.

### Repair: preventive $k_i$ and restorative $k_\mathrm{rec}$ {#sec-repair}

Fast refolding is now the instantaneous equilibrium $\varphi_d$, so the single
old refold knob splits into two mechanistically distinct axes:

- **Preventive $k_i$** — the leak rate from the unfolded pool into $I_r$. Lowering it
  is chaperone-like stabilisation of the intermediate.
- **Restorative $k_\mathrm{rec}$** — resynthesis speed of $I_r$, calibrated by the
  3–5 d rebound. It is gated off above $T_\mathrm{rep,cut}$ (repurposed `t_rep_cut`,
  `m_rep`) because the synthesis machinery itself fails when too hot
  ([`leaf_model.cpp`](../src/leaf_model.cpp), `k_rec_eff`):
  $$
  k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}(T_\ell)=k_\mathrm{rec}\,\sigma\!\big(-m_\mathrm{rep}(T_\ell-T_\mathrm{rep,cut})\big),
  \qquad \sigma(x)=\tfrac{1}{1+e^{-x}} .
  $$ {#eq-krec}

Above $T_\mathrm{rep,cut}$, $\varphi_d\to1$ *and* recovery shuts off, so $I_r$ accrues
unchecked and matures into $I_p$ — the runaway that yields heatwave lethality.

---

## Slow ODE states: acclimation $A$ and the damage pools $I_r,I_p$ {#sec-accl}

Four slow ODE state variables are appended to the TF24t strategy state vector
([`tf24t_strategy.cpp`](../src/tf24t_strategy.cpp), `compute_rates`):
`acclim_thermostab` ($A$), `damage_recoverable` ($I_r$), `damage_permanent` ($I_p$),
and the diagnostic `mean_leaf_temp` ($\overline{T_\ell}$, §[-@sec-meanT]). The first
three values are fed into the leaf each step ($I_r,I_p$ before the reused TF24 rates
run, so the capacity discount sees them); $\varphi_d$ and
$k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}$ are read back at the operating-point $T_\ell$ to form
the damage rates.

**Acclimation.** A single thermostability state relaxes toward a heat-driven forcing:

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}A}{\mathrm{d}t}
 = D\,\big[\alpha\,\mathrm{sp}\!\big(T - T_\mathrm{accl}\big) - \beta A\big],
\qquad
\mathrm{sp}(x) = \tfrac{1}{s}\log\!\big(1 + e^{s x}\big),
$$ {#eq-accl}

where $T$ is the (midday) `air_temp` driver, $\mathrm{sp}$ is the
softplus ($C^1$) replacement for $\max(0,x)$ (sharpness $s$), and
$D=365.25\ \mathrm{d\,yr^{-1}}$ converts the day⁻¹ kinetics to the SCM's yearly clock
(§[-@sec-merged-numerics]). $A$ feeds the $T_\mathrm{opt}$/onset shift (@eq-dtopt).

**Damage cascade.** The two pools draw from the transiently-unfolded substrate
$\varphi_d$ and mature/recover on separate timescales:

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}I_r}{\mathrm{d}t}=D\,\Big[k_i\,\varphi_d(T_\ell)\,(1-I_r-I_p)
 - \big(k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}+k_\mathrm{mat}\big)\,I_r\Big],
\qquad
\frac{\mathrm{d}I_p}{\mathrm{d}t}=D\,k_\mathrm{mat}\,I_r-\frac{g}{L}\,I_p .
$$ {#eq-cascade}

The $(1-I_r-I_p)$ factor confines fresh damage to not-yet-damaged protein, bounding
$I_r+I_p\le1$ without a clamp. The **maturation coupling** is the central emergent
behaviour: the permanent fraction of an insult is
$\approx k_\mathrm{mat}/(k_\mathrm{rec}+k_\mathrm{mat})$, so prompt restorative repair
both rebounds faster *and* leaves a lower permanent floor.

**Permanent clearance by dilution.** $I_p$ is an intensive fraction; with unbiased
senescence the shed-tissue terms cancel and only clean new leaf dilutes it, so
$g/L$ is the **gross leaf-area production rate** over leaf area. The implementation
uses $g/L = k_l + \max(0,\dot A_\ell)/A_\ell$ (leaf turnover rate $k_l$ in the mature
limit, faster while the canopy expands; $\dot A_\ell$ recovered from the height rate).
$g/L$ is already per-year, so it takes no $D$ factor.

**Equilibrium and seeding.** $A$ is **seeded at its equilibrium**
$A^\star=(\alpha/\beta)\,\mathrm{sp}(T-T_\mathrm{accl})$ (the $D$ cancels in the ratio)
for the birth environment, with $I_r=I_p=0$ (fresh recruits have undamaged leaves), so
there is no cold-start transient (`set_initial_states`).

> **Timescale (reconciled).** Kinetics are stated in day⁻¹ and converted to the
> yearly clock by $D$. This makes $I_r$ (~4 d) a genuinely fast mode relative to the
> demographic clock; it is integrated faithfully as an ODE, at a real cost in
> integration steps (§[-@sec-merged-numerics]). The rate constants and cost scales
> remain calibration targets.

### Running-mean leaf temperature $\overline{T_\ell}$ {#sec-meanT}

A fourth state, `mean_leaf_temp`, tracks the plant's average growing temperature as
an exponential moving average of the **operating-point** leaf temperature
$T_\mathrm{op}$ (the stored `Leaf::T_op_`, §[-@sec-energy], exported as the aux
`operating_leaf_temp`):

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}\,\overline{T_\ell}}{\mathrm{d}t}
  = D\,k_{\overline{T}}\,\bigl(T_\mathrm{op} - \overline{T_\ell}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-meanT}

with decay rate $k_{\overline{T}}$ (`k_mean_leaf_temp`, day⁻¹; $D=365.25$ puts it on
the yearly clock). Its steady state is $T_\mathrm{op}$ and its memory time constant
is $1/k_{\overline{T}}$ (default $\approx 30$ d). It is seeded at the birth air
temperature (the operating point is not solved until the first `compute_rates`).

**This state is purely diagnostic**: it is read *from* $T_\mathrm{op}$ but is not
read *by* the damage or acclimation machinery — it does not shift $\Delta S$, enter
$\varphi_d$, or change any other rate. It exists so the temperature history a plant
has actually experienced is available on the R side as an ODE output. (Driving
acclimation off $\overline{T_\ell}$ instead of the instantaneous driver — a
Knauer-style running-mean forcing — is a possible future change, noted in
`notes/atls/knauer-2023-temperature-acclimation.md`.)

---

## Carbon costs of thermal strategy {#sec-cost}

Costs live in two places, matching the physics.

### Leaf-level respiration

Added to dark respiration $R_d$ (µmol CO₂ m⁻² s⁻¹; base $R_d = 0.015\,V_\mathrm{cmax}$)
on the damage path ([`leaf_model.cpp`](../src/leaf_model.cpp),
`update_temperature_dependent_params`):

$$
R_d \;\mathrel{+}=\;
\underbrace{c_\mathrm{acclim}\,A}_{\text{acclim. maintenance}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{c_\mathrm{rep,maint}\,k_\mathrm{rec}
 + c_\mathrm{prot}\max(0,k_{i,\mathrm{ref}}-k_i)}_{\text{repair + protection maintenance}}
\;+\;
\underbrace{c_\mathrm{rep,flux}\,k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}\,I_r}_{\text{repair activity}} .
$$ {#eq-Rd}

Standing maintenance is paid whether or not used — for resynthesis *capacity*
($k_\mathrm{rec}$) and for the *protection* level (chaperone-like stabilisation,
i.e. lowering $k_i$ below a reference $k_{i,\mathrm{ref}}$). Repair *activity* is paid
in proportion to protein actually rebuilt ($k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}\,I_r$,
replacing the as-built $k_{r1}(1-N)$).

### Whole-plant net production

The TF24t strategy overrides net mass production to subtract two costs that are not
leaf-local respiration ([`tf24t_strategy.cpp`](../src/tf24t_strategy.cpp),
`net_mass_production_dt`):

$$
\dot m_\mathrm{net}^{\,\mathrm{TF24t}} = \dot m_\mathrm{net}^{\,\mathrm{TF24}}
 - C_\mathrm{build} - C_\mathrm{induct}.
$$

- **Construction cost** (constitutive tolerance) collapses to *one* axis — the single
  thermostability offset — amortised through leaf turnover $\tau_\ell(\text{mass}_\ell)$:
  $$
  C_\mathrm{build} = c_\mathrm{build}\,\max(0,\Delta T_\mathrm{opt,0})\,\tau_\ell .
  $$
  You only pay for thermostability bought *above* the intrinsic optimum, so a default
  TF24t pays no construction cost.
- **Induction cost** (acclimation), proportional to the smoothed positive build rate
  of the single state:
  $$
  C_\mathrm{induct} = c_\mathrm{induct}\,\mathrm{pos}(\dot A),
  \qquad \mathrm{pos}(x)=\tfrac12\big(x + \sqrt{x^2+\varepsilon^2}\big),
  $$
  a $C^\infty$ positive part matching the form TF24 uses for net production.

Avoidance carries **no new cost term**: its water use is already priced by the Sperry
hydraulic pathway.

---

## The optimiser feedback: why avoidance is self-selecting {#sec-feedback}

The leaf chooses its stem water potential $\psi_\mathrm{stem}$ to maximise profit,

$$
\Pi(\psi_\mathrm{stem}) = A\big(T_\ell(E(\psi_\mathrm{stem}))\big) - (\text{hydraulic risk cost}),
$$

solved by `find_root_collar_psi`. The coupling chain closes the loop:

$$
\psi_\mathrm{stem} \;\to\; E \;\xrightarrow{\text{@eq-tleaf}}\; T_\ell
\;\xrightarrow{\text{@eq-phid}}\; \varphi_d \;\to\; \dot I_r \;\to\; (1-I_r-I_p)J_\mathrm{max} \;\to\; A \;\to\; \Pi .
$$

A more-transpiring (or better-coupled, smaller-$d$) candidate runs a cooler midday
$T_\ell$, lowering $\varphi_d$ and hence the damage flux into $I_r$ — so over time it
carries less lasting damage, keeps more capacity, and the optimiser *values* cooling
directly, with no separate avoidance machinery. Forcing the PM energy balance on gives
a real operating-point $T_\ell$, and $\varphi_d$ evaluated there makes avoidance a
self-selecting outcome of the existing profit maximisation.

---

## Parameters and defaults {#sec-params}

Thermal / acclimation / cost parameters exposed on the `TF24t` strategy
([`tf24t_strategy.h`](../inst/include/plant/models/tf24t_strategy.h)); leaf-side
mirrors carry a trailing underscore.

| Symbol | Code | Default | Units | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\Delta T_\mathrm{opt,0}$ | `topt_offset` | 0 | °C | constitutive thermostability shift ($T_\mathrm{opt}$ + onset) |
| $k_i$ | `k_i` | 0.5 | day⁻¹ | preventive leak $\varphi_d\to I_r$ |
| $k_\mathrm{rec}$ | `k_rec` | 0.25 | day⁻¹ | restorative resynthesis of $I_r$ (3–5 d rebound) |
| $k_\mathrm{mat}$ | `k_mat` | 0.02 | day⁻¹ | maturation $I_r\to I_p$ |
| $m_\mathrm{rep}$ | `m_rep` | 0.4 | °C⁻¹ | repair-collapse switch slope |
| $T_\mathrm{rep,cut}$ | `t_rep_cut` | 45 | °C | resynthesis shut-off temperature |
| $\Delta T_\mathrm{opt,max}$ | `dTopt_max` | 6 | °C | max acclimation rise in $T_\mathrm{opt}$ |
| $K_A$ | `K_A` | 1.0 | — | half-saturation of acclimation response |
| $\alpha$ | `alpha` | 0.02 | — | acclimation forcing gain |
| $\beta$ | `beta` | 0.01 | day⁻¹ | acclimation decay rate |
| $T_\mathrm{accl}$ | `t_accl` | 30 | °C | acclimation forcing threshold |
| $s$ | `softplus_s` | 1.0 | °C⁻¹ | softplus sharpness |
| $k_{\overline{T}}$ | `k_mean_leaf_temp` | 0.0333 | day⁻¹ | running-mean leaf-temp decay rate (~30 d memory; diagnostic, §[-@sec-meanT]) |
| $c_\mathrm{acclim}$ | `c_acclim_maint` | 0.02 | — | acclimation maintenance ($R_d$, per unit $A$) |
| $c_\mathrm{rep,maint}$ | `c_repair_maint` | $10^{-5}$ | — | repair maintenance ($R_d$, per day⁻¹ of $k_\mathrm{rec}$) |
| $c_\mathrm{prot}$ | `c_protect_maint` | $10^{-5}$ | — | protection maintenance ($R_d$, per day⁻¹ of $k_{i,\mathrm{ref}}-k_i$) |
| $c_\mathrm{rep,flux}$ | `c_repair_flux` | $10^{-4}$ | — | repair activity ($R_d$, per day⁻¹ of resynthesis flux) |
| $c_\mathrm{build}$ | `c_build` | 0.02 | °C⁻¹ | construction premium on leaf turnover, per °C thermostability |
| $c_\mathrm{induct}$ | `c_accl_induct` | 0.01 | — | induction cost, biomass per unit positive $\dot A$ |
| $\varepsilon$ | `induct_eps` | $10^{-4}$ | — | smoothing of the positive-part of $\dot A$ |

Fixed leaf-side constants (not R-settable): $k_{i,\mathrm{ref}}=0.5$ day⁻¹
(no-extra-protection reference), survival floor $10^{-6}$, $D=365.25$ day yr⁻¹.

Fixed leaf physical constants ([`leaf_model.h`](../inst/include/plant/leaf_model.h)):
$R=8.314$, $T_0=273.15$, $\lambda=2.45\times10^6$ J kg⁻¹, $\rho c_p=1200$ J m⁻³ K⁻¹,
$a_\mathrm{sw}=2$, $\eta_\mathrm{par}=4.57$ µmol J⁻¹, $L_\mathrm{net}=-40$ W m⁻²,
$C_{r_a}=200$ (fixed fallback $r_a=50$ s m⁻¹), $T_\ell\in[-40,70]$ °C.
Peaked-Arrhenius: $V_\mathrm{cmax}$ $(E_a,H_d,\Delta S)=(60000,200000,650)$;
$J_\mathrm{max}$ $(30000,200000,650)$.

## Numerical-stability contract {#sec-numerics}

The layer feeds the ODE integrator and the `run_mutant` replay cache, where a single
non-finite value poisons the whole SCM run. The equations are therefore built to a
finite-output contract:

- **$C^1$ everywhere.** All temperature/threshold responses are smooth in drivers and
  traits: the deactivation fraction $\varphi_d$ and the repair gate
  $k_\mathrm{rec}^\mathrm{eff}$ (logistic), softplus forcing, smooth positive part
  $\mathrm{pos}(\cdot)$. No `if`-branch on a driver/trait *value* inside a response.
- **Bounded / saturating forms.** $\Delta T_\mathrm{opt}(A)$ saturates;
  $\varphi_d\in[0,1]$; the $(1-I_r-I_p)$ factor bounds the pools without a clamp;
  acclimation self-limits via $-\beta A$ decay. Every expression has a finite limit as
  any input $\to\pm\infty$.
- **Guarded transcendentals.** Logistic, $\varphi_d$'s $K$, and softplus arguments are
  clamped to $|{\cdot}|\le30$ before `exp`; `log1p` used near 0.
- **Protected domains.** $K_A>0$ guards @eq-dtopt; the $\Delta S$ shifts (capacity and
  damage-onset) are clamped via $T_K\in[250,350]$ so the curves stay peaked; $T_\ell$
  is clamped to $[-40,70]$ °C.
- **Survival floor.** The discount $1-I_r-I_p$ is floored at $10^{-6}$, so a fully
  damaged leaf keeps a negligible-but-positive capacity and the FvCB colimitation /
  $\psi$-stem solve stay well-conditioned as $I_r+I_p\to1$.
- **A genuine fast mode (documented cost).** Reconciling the day⁻¹ kinetics to the
  yearly clock makes $I_r$ (~4 d) a fast ODE mode relative to the demographic clock.
  It is integrated faithfully, but forces small adaptive steps — each running a PM
  $\psi$-stem solve — so SCM runs are materially slower than the as-built quasi-steady
  layer, and a leaf pinned at sustained lethal heat (never culled) drives $I_r+I_p\to1$
  and the step size very small. Real SCM runs cull dying plants and complete; tests
  exercise the physics with single-evaluation rate checks and moderate integrations
  rather than pathological lethal-heat integrations.

---

## Revision history: from the as-built layer to this model {#sec-merged}

::: {.callout-note}
## Status: implemented
This section is a design-history note. The body above (§[-@sec-capacity]–§[-@sec-numerics])
now describes the model **as implemented** on `feature/tf24-atls-thermal-damage` after
the *merged revision*. The **as-built** layer it superseded used an instantaneous,
reversible Lumry–Eyring factor $N=k_r/(k_r+k_d)$ (a second high-$T$ discount on top of
the peaked-Arrhenius deactivation) and two independent acclimation states
(`acclim_topt`, `acclim_tcrit`). Full phase-by-phase history lives in
`notes/atls/implementation-plan.md`.
:::

The revision made two structural changes:

1. **Merged the two reversible declines into one.** The high-$T$ decline was
   represented twice — once by the peaked-Arrhenius deactivation and again by the
   $N\rightleftharpoons D$ switch, both discounting $J_\mathrm{max}$. The revision derives
   the deactivated fraction $\varphi_d=K/(1+K)$ from the *same* Medlyn $K(T)$
   (§[-@sec-phid]), so the reversible response is counted once and the damage onset
   becomes **emergent** at $\approx H_d/\Delta S\approx34.5$ °C. Removed: `tcrit_0`,
   `m_switch`, `dTcrit_max`, `k_d1_0`, `k_r1_0`.

2. **Gave damage lasting memory.** $N$ was memoryless (a cooled leaf rebounded
   instantly), whereas heat-shock recovery takes 3–5 days and a fraction never repairs.
   The revision adds two slow pools (§[-@sec-cascade]): recoverable $I_r$ (resynthesised
   over ~4 d) and permanent $I_p$ (cleared only by new-leaf dilution). Both capacities
   carry the $(1-I_r-I_p)$ discount. Added: $k_i$, $k_\mathrm{rec}$, $k_\mathrm{mat}$;
   the old repair-shutoff (`t_rep_cut`, `m_rep`) is repurposed to gate $k_\mathrm{rec}$.

The **maturation coupling** (permanent fraction of an insult
$\approx k_\mathrm{mat}/(k_\mathrm{rec}+k_\mathrm{mat})$; §[-@sec-cascade]) is the central
emergent behaviour: prompt restorative repair prevents permanent scarring. The two
acclimation states merged into one thermostability state $A$ shifting $\Delta S$
(moving $T_\mathrm{opt}$ and onset together, near-rigid). Net ODE state change: the two
as-built states (`acclim_topt`, `acclim_tcrit`) became three
(`acclim_thermostab`, `damage_recoverable`, `damage_permanent`) at `TF24t@v3.2`, and a
fourth diagnostic state (`mean_leaf_temp`, the running-mean leaf temperature,
§[-@sec-meanT]) was subsequently added at `thermal_revision = 3` (`TF24t@v3.3`).

### Timescales, calibration, and the near-rigid caveat {#sec-merged-numerics}

Mode timescales after the day→year reconciliation (§[-@sec-accl]): $\varphi_d(T_\ell)$
is algebraic (the fast equilibrium), $I_r\sim$ 4 d, $A\sim$ 100 d, $I_p\sim$ turnover
(months). $I_r$ is thus a genuinely fast ODE mode on the yearly demographic clock — see
the performance note in §[-@sec-numerics]. Calibration anchors are largely independent:
$k_\mathrm{rec}$ from the 3–5 d rebound; $k_\mathrm{mat}$ from the permanent residue per
event; $k_i$ from damage magnitude after a known heat dose; thermostability from the
observed $T_\mathrm{opt}$ shift. All ship as modest nonzero **calibration targets**.

**Near-rigid, not exact.** $T_\mathrm{opt,K}=H_d/(\Delta S-\mathrm{corr})$ carries the
extra $\mathrm{corr}=R\ln(E_a/(H_d-E_a))$ term while the onset $H_d/\Delta S$ does not,
so shifting $\Delta S$ translates peak and onset by *nearly* — not exactly — the same
amount. Thermostability is a near-rigid translation of the whole curve.
